title: Your Lie in April?  In July?!?  Groundbreaking #WestEnd #London #Lond...
transcript: I've always thought that when it comes to adapting anime into live action, theatre is probably the best medium, because theatre, like anime, has this heightened sense of emotion that you just don't get in other live action mediums like film and T. V. I think that's why we see so many live action anime adaptations fail, because they're just not able to capture the energy and spirit of the source material. However, we've seen tremendous success in adapting anime to the stage, most recently with Spirited Away and My Neighbor Todoroki. And in my opinion, your lie in April is no exception. Well, definitely not a perfect musical. I do think that it perfectly captures the tone and spirit of anime. I can definitely see how if you're not a fan of anime, this is not a show that would resonate with you. I myself, I'm definitely not a huge anime fan, but I have watched a few animes and I do enjoy them, and so for me I totally got what they were going for here and it totally worked for me. If you haven't seen the anime, your lie in April tells the story of two musicians, a violinist and pianist, who come into each other's lives and in the process change them. Is at its core a Love Story and also a very emotional one. I definitely found myself tearing up at the end, and I think a lot of people in the audience did. Too so while I personally found Act 1 to be a little bit slow, once we got to Act two and they introduced the stakes, I was completely enthralled. The music is by Frank Wildhorn, who personally I find a little hit or miss, but I am a big fan of his score for Death Note The Musical, which I find incredibly underrated. I was very excited to see another anime adaptation from him, and while I definitely enjoyed a lot of the score, I did find some of it to be a little bit samey. It's definitely very ballad heavy, which personally I don't love in my musical theater, but there are definitely some really gorgeous melodies, and when it is trying to elicit emotion from you, it is 100% successful at that. I think the overall production is just fine. The set is very minimal and nothing special, but I thought all of the performances were really fantastic and like I said before, capture that anime tone perfectly. So while I had some issues with the pacing in Act 1, because Act 2 was so emotionally satisfying and the performances were so great, I still really enjoyed the show overall. I'm gonna give it 3.5 stars and I would recommend checking this out if you are in London, especially if you are a fan of either anime or the romcom genre. They recently announced that they're going to be closing early on August 11th, which is a shame, so Definitely be sure to check it out before them. Tickets are super cheap.
